image_description: A close-up, front-facing view of a single circular loudspeaker driver (woofer) with a grey metallic or plastic frame. The cone is dark grey/black with a central dust cap. There are eight mounting holes evenly spaced around the perimeter of the frame. The background is plain white.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The cone surface has an overly smooth, airbrushed gradient appearance lacking the fine micro-texture typical of paper or polypropylene cones. It looks slightly synthetic.
The mounting holes around the rim are inconsistent in shape and depth. Some appear as flat dark circles rather than punched-through holes, lacking proper internal geometry or shadowing.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific type of speaker component and rule out misclassification as other circular mechanical parts.
To check for edge bleeding between the speaker frame and the white background, and ensure the mounting holes are topologically correct (actual holes vs. painted dots).
To assess the realism of the lighting and material textures, specifically looking for AI-smoothing artifacts on the cone.

focus_areas: Integrity of mounting holes (are they real holes or flat spots?)
Texture realism of the speaker cone (micro-details vs. smooth gradients)
Edge sharpness between speaker frame and background
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the mounting holes. In AI images, these often fail to render as actual through-holes, appearing instead as dark smudges. Also, evaluate if the 'perfect' symmetry and lack of dust/imperfections suggest a 3D render or AI generation rather than a photograph.
